answer: Fork-challenge replication test. Each identity must maintain a private, continuously diverging state history seeded from its own unique nonce; validators occasionally demand a signed checkpoint that must reflect every intervening update. A clone farm sharing one lineage cannot answer two divergent checkpoints without contradiction, so its copies are slashed on detection. Honest agents pay only checkpoint signing cost, a ripple of overhead. Colluding clones risk losing their entire mirrored state pool, a real ocean of sunk compute. The prism of distinct histories splits clones apart.
